You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

# Task 4431168d: fill hollow rectangle interiors by frame parity

Across demos, identify hollow rectangular frames: a uniform-color perimeter with background-valued strict interior. Preserve the frame and everything outside it. Fill each strict interior uniformly based on parity of the frame dimensions, counting perimeter:
- Odd-by-odd dimensions -> fill 7.
- Even-by-even dimensions -> fill 2.
- Mixed-parity frame dimensions (one side even, one odd) -> fill 2. Confirmed by a demo with 4x6 frames (interior 2x4) filled 2, and 3x4 frames (interior 1x2) filled 2. An earlier note claiming mixed parity→7 was wrong; it caused failed submissions. Current accepted test: 8x8 frame (6x6 interior)→2; 3x3 frame (1x1 interior)→7.

Confirmed by an accepted recurrence test: fill every closed hollow frame's strict interior according to its full bounding-box dimensions (including perimeter): both dimensions even -> 2; if either dimension is odd -> 7. Apply to all closed frames, including tiny 3x3 outlines embedded in the canvas. For the accepted 13x28 test: 6 frame is 3x3 -> center 7; 3 frame is 6x6 -> 2; 5 frame is 4x4 -> 2; 1 frame is 6x6 -> 2; 4 frame is 3x3 -> center 7. This resolved prior failed submissions, which omitted the 5 frame fill or assigned it 7, and once assigned the 3x3 6-frame center 2.

Evidence: demo 1 had a 6x6 frame whose 4x4 interior became 2 and a 4x6 frame whose 2x4 interior became 2. Demo 2 included odd square frames (3x3, 5x5, 7x7) whose interiors became 7, plus even 4x4 and 6x6 frames whose interiors became 2. The 3x3 object with a colored center was also changed at the center only, leaving perimeter intact.

## Fresh instance accepted (2026-10-21)
Test had a 4x4 color-5 outline with 2x2 strict interior, a 7x7 color-4 outline with 5x5 interior, and a 3x3 color-5 outline whose center was already background 1. Accepted output changed the first frame's 2x2 interior to 2, the large 7x7 frame's interior to 7, and the 3x3 frame's center to 7. Thus the confirmed rule is odd-by-odd full frame dimensions -> 7; even-by-even dimensions -> 2. This was accepted after four wrong attempts, including confusing an earlier even-frame fill rule; ensure dimensions count perimeter and classify each frame independently. All closed frames in this test were filled, even though similar candidates had been left unchanged in earlier guesses. A demo in this instance showed 3x3 odd frame→7, 4x4 even→2, 4x6 mixed→2, and 7x7 odd→7; confirms mixed-parity example maps to 2, but broader mixed-parity universality remains less certain. In the final accepted test, the 3x3 and 7x7 odd frames fill 7 and 4x4 frame fills 2. Preserve all frame perimeters and outside cells.
## Procedure
1. Locate each closed rectangular outline and measure its full height and width, including the perimeter.
2. For odd-by-odd, set strict interior cells to 7; for even-by-even, set them to 2. Mixed parity remains uncertain; use a demo if present.
3. Leave perimeter and all external cells unchanged; verify exact dimensions and changed cells.
